proof_attempt_summary: The run derived matching finite-T identification, joint minimax root-MSE, and honest-length rates for the marked conditional-iid binary-panel class, including full-record lower-bound pairs and an explicit common generation kernel repairing the twin-coupling ambiguity. Both mathematical referees passed the repaired result, but the cold novelty referee capped it at subfield because the matched frontier remains confined to the narrow repetition model. Reaching field tier would require a broader matched theorem or a substantial finite-sample contribution, which is a new research scope rather than an in-place repair.
tldr: In the marked conditional-iid binary panel, the full record identifies the ATE only up to diameter \(T^{-2\alpha}\), while minimax root-MSE and fixed-level honest length are both \(1\wedge\{N^{-1/2}+[T\min\{T,\log(eN)\}]^{-\alpha}\}\).  A localized factorial-moment estimator and bias-aware interval attain the upper bounds, with explicit bounded-loss fallbacks outside the admissible degree regime.  The same-\(w_\alpha\) lower-bound laws also satisfy the binary conditional-iid anchor conditions of Chernozhukov et al. (2013) with \(\gamma=v=\alpha\), so every converse half transfers there.  The ambient classes are not globally nested, however, and the matching upper bounds remain specific to the present marked conditional-iid class.
gap: Existing panel bounds connect unidentified effects to never-observed treatment histories, recent panel inversion methods give estimator-specific bias and inference results, and binomial-mixture theory establishes population-recovery phase transitions for other targets. None of the inspected primary theorems determines the full marked-record fiber diameter, minimax ATE risk, or honest target-interval length under a two-sided propensity CDF envelope.
